high.title: Bank of Korea Holds Policy Rate Steady at 2.50%, Signals Rate Hikes Ahead as Inflation Pressure Mounts
high.summary: The Bank of Korea maintained its benchmark rate at 2.50% on May 28th under new Governor Shin Hyun-song's leadership, but signaled a hawkish shift with rate hikes expected ahead. The central bank upgraded its 2026 growth outlook to 2.6% while facing mounting inflation pressures that accelerated to the fastest pace in 21 months in April. Markets are pricing in at least two rate increases to 3.0% this year as policymakers gain scope to combat rising inflation amid resilient economic growth. The decision comes as South Korea enjoys record current account surpluses yet sees the won persistently weakening above 1,500 per dollar, defying traditional economic relationships. For bond investors, the hawkish pivot suggests upward pressure on yields across the curve, while FX traders should monitor how aggressive BOK rhetoric becomes in upcoming meetings. The central bank's ability to raise rates without derailing growth will be crucial for KRW strength and government bond performance.

high.title: Dollar-Won Falls Below 1,500 on US-Iran Ceasefire Progress, Closes at 1,494.00
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate broke below the psychologically important 1,500 level in overnight trading, closing at 1,494.00 won after falling 7.20 won from the Seoul market close. The sharp move came on reports that the US and Iran agreed to a ceasefire memorandum of understanding, with only President Trump's approval remaining. However, Iranian semi-official media later disputed claims of a finalized agreement, suggesting volatility could continue. This represents a significant technical break for the won, which had traded above 1,500 for six consecutive sessions despite Korea's record current account surplus. For FX traders, the 1,500 level had become a key resistance turned support - the break below signals potential for further won strength if geopolitical tensions continue to ease. Oil price impacts from Middle East developments will also influence Korea's import costs and inflation outlook, making this a key variable for BOK policy timing.

high.title: South Korean Banks' BIS Capital Ratio Falls to 15.64% in Q1 on Currency Impact
high.summary: Korean banks' capital adequacy ratios declined in Q1 as the BIS ratio fell to 15.64% from 15.83% at year-end, driven by increased lending assets and rising exchange rates. The common equity tier 1 (CET1) ratio dropped to 13.41% from 13.50%. The Financial Supervisory Service attributed the decline to risk-weighted assets growing faster than common equity capital, with currency fluctuations playing a significant role. While ratios remain well above regulatory minimums, the downward trend reflects both credit growth and FX volatility impacts on bank balance sheets. This data is crucial for investors as it indicates potential constraints on bank lending capacity and dividend policies if the trend continues. Combined with rising NPL ratios that hit 0.6% as household and corporate bad debt increased, the banking sector faces headwinds that could influence BOK monetary policy deliberations and Korean financial sector performance.

medium.title: Foreign Investors Offload $3 Billion in Korean Stocks in April, Extending Four-Month Selling Streak
medium.summary: Foreign investors net sold 4.046 trillion won ($3 billion) in Korean equities during April, marking four consecutive months of outflows. The selling was concentrated in KOSPI (3.638 trillion won) with additional KOSDAQ outflows of 408 billion won. However, foreign bond holdings shifted to net buying, suggesting a rotation rather than complete Korean asset rejection. This continued equity outflow pressure explains persistent won weakness despite strong fundamentals.

medium.title: National Pension Service Raises Domestic Stock Target to 20.8% by Year-End
medium.summary: The National Pension Service increased its domestic equity target allocation from 14.9% to 20.8% by year-end, effective from June when the rebalancing moratorium expires. Officials cited "Korean market rerating" and structural changes following Commercial Act revisions. NPS Chairman Kim Seong-joo denied this was meant to prop up stocks, emphasizing long-term investment objectives. This could provide significant buying support for Korean equities in coming months.

medium.title: Bank of Korea Joins 'Project Agora' Cross-Border Payment Initiative
medium.summary: The BOK announced participation in Project Agora, a BIS-led initiative exploring tokenized bank deposits and wholesale CBDCs for cross-border payments. The project includes central banks from six major economies and over 40 global financial institutions. Live transaction tests are planned ahead, potentially modernizing Korea's international payment infrastructure and supporting won internationalization efforts.

medium.title: US Treasury Auctions Show Solid Demand Despite Higher Yields
medium.summary: US 5-year notes auctioned at 4.182% (up 22.7bp from previous month) and 7-year notes at 4.290% (up 11.5bp), both showing solid demand metrics. Foreign participation in the 7-year auction hit highest since December 2024. Rising US yields create headwinds for Korean government bonds and may influence BOK policy timing as rate differentials narrow.

medium.title: BOK Analysis: Korea's Non-IT Export Market Share Resilient Despite US-China Tariffs
medium.summary: Bank of Korea research shows Korean non-IT exports fell 12.8% to the US following tariffs on China, but market share loss was limited to 0.4 percentage points—outperforming China, Japan, and Germany. This export resilience supports Korea's current account strength and provides fundamental backing for won stability despite recent weakness.
